rules.title: Los Angeles RSO annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: For RSO-covered units, rent may be raised only once every 12 months, by the allowable rent increase percentage. Since February 2, 2026 landlords can no longer add an extra percentage for utilities. Rent may be reset to market rate only in listed cases, such as when the tenant voluntarily moves out or is evicted for cause.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by the published allowable rent increase percentage

coverage_conditions.summary: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28. Covers apartments, duplexes, ADUs/JADUs, hotel/rooming house units occupied over 30 days, mobile homes, and similar. Condominiums and townhomes are covered, but their rent is not regulated for tenancies commenced after December 31, 1995.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Condominium and townhome rent amount not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995. Luxury exemption available by application.

rules.exemptions: Units built after October 1, 1978; condominiums/townhomes with tenancies commenced after December 31, 1995 (rent amount not regulated); luxury exemption by application to LAHD.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO); LAMC § 151.28 (replacement units)
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

rules.title: RSO additional tenant rent increase (10%)
rules.requirement: Since February 2, 2026 the extra 10% increase for an added dependent is no longer permitted. A 10% increase is still allowed for an additional tenant who is not a dependent, if the landlord raises the rent within 60 days of learning of that tenant.
rules.key_value: 10% for an additional non-dependent tenant, within 60 days of learning of the tenant

coverage_conditions.summary: RSO-covered rental units (generally built on or before October 1, 1978).

rules.quoted_span: However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

rules.title: RSO just cause eviction reasons
rules.requirement: RSO-covered tenancies may be ended only for enumerated at-fault reasons (e.g. nonpayment, lease violation, nuisance) or no-fault reasons (e.g. owner or family move-in, resident manager, demolition, government order, conversion to affordable housing). Termination notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service on the tenant.

coverage_conditions.summary: RSO-covered rental units (generally built on or before October 1, 1978). Non-RSO units fall under the separate Just Cause Ordinance.

rules.interaction: Properties not covered by the RSO still have rights and responsibilities under the city's Just Cause Ordinance.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO); LAMC 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5 (filing of notices)
rules.quoted_span: The owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit

rules.title: RSO relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.requirement: No-fault evictions of RSO tenants require payment of tenant relocation assistance. The landlord must file a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and give 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120 days or up to a 1-year extension).
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance payment; 30-day and 60-day written notices
